payload.selection_rationale: One proposal, so this is selection against the survey, not a choice between designs. I took it whole and changed three things. It matches the measured code: C1 and C2 are built (ChildrenLargestFirst, ChildRow.Share, RolledOnDisk), so no Core code is written and the slice is App-only plus test-side hook code. It avoids both no-go spikes (live refresh: 84 ms median, 866 ms UI gap; mid-scan shares: child above parent 10-21 times per scan) by building the tree only from the finished ScanResult.Store, which is what owed row 1 says ("when it finishes"). It uses the one tree configuration that was measured: a stock TreeView, virtualizing, Recycling, Pixel scroll. That config peaked at 816 MiB with the store loaded and stayed flat over 5 collapse/expand cycles of a 100k folder. U-001 measured a 230 ms median cold 100k expand. It respects Q-016 (the report never holds a listing) by putting the listing in the hook's own log. It reuses the FsaWindowHook, WindowCases.ps1 and StallRig infrastructure already in the stack block. Changes I made: (1) the hook reads the rendered TextBlock text of realized containers, not node properties by reflection. XAML binds directly with no converter, and WPF binding failures are silent, so a node-property check would pass with a blank column. (2) Row 5 asserts every one of the 5 opens, and open 1 (cold: JIT, sort, node build) is logged apart from opens 2-5, which reuse the cached array. (3) The claim that the old store is released before the next scan (the proposal's must-verify) becomes a case with a WeakReference, not a hope. Nothing at project scope was left open and decided here: language, runtime, UI, tests and packaging are all in the stack block. TreeView versus a custom control is component design, so `stack_chosen` is empty. Rejected prior art: FreeSize's live-growing tree, which both spikes measured failing on this Core.

components.name: FolderTreeNode
components.responsibility: One displayed tree row. It holds the ScanStore reference, its entry index and the ChildRow values (OnDisk, Share). Name and sizes are read from the store when a row is drawn, not copied into the node. It implements INotifyPropertyChanged for IsExpanded and Children. A folder with ChildCount > 0 starts with a shared one-item placeholder child so the expander shows. On the first IsExpanded=true it calls store.ChildrenLargestFirst(entry), builds one node array in that order, and replaces Children once (a single reset). The array is kept until the next scan starts. Files, links and folders with ChildCount 0 are leaf rows with no placeholder and no expander.
components.key_interactions: Reads ScanStore.ChildrenLargestFirst / RolledOnDisk / RolledSize (src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/ScanStore.Rollup.cs:19,27,57) and Name / Kind / ChildCount / GetPath (ScanStore.cs:80,87,135,138). XAML binds to its display properties with no converter. Root(ScanStore) labels the root with GetPath(root) and gives it no share.

components.name: FolderTreeRowText
components.responsibility: Formats a row: on-disk size and size, using the same size formatting as TopLevelRowText; the share as Share*100 to one decimal place plus ' %', using the same culture rule as the existing size text; and the bar width as Share times a fixed track width. A parent with 0 rolled on-disk gives '0.0 %' and a zero-width bar. The root has no share and no bar.
components.key_interactions: Reuses the size-formatting helper behind TopLevelRowText.FiguresOf (:34-44). If FiguresOf only returns a joined string, extract the size formatter rather than parsing it. TopLevelRowText.cs:10 ('no percentages') is left alone: it still describes the flat list mid-scan and after Cancel.

components.name: FolderTree (TreeView)
components.responsibility: A virtualized TreeView in the same grid cell as TopLevelList (MainWindow.xaml:225-240), collapsed until a scan completes. One HierarchicalDataTemplate with a fixed row height. The row is a DockPanel: the numeric columns (bar, percentage, size, on-disk) are docked right at fixed widths and the name fills the rest, so the columns stay aligned at every depth. A header row above the tree uses the same right-docked widths. The ItemContainerStyle binds TreeViewItem.IsExpanded TwoWay to FolderTreeNode.IsExpanded. It sets VirtualizingPanel.IsVirtualizing=True, VirtualizationMode=Recycling and ScrollUnit=Pixel (the measured configuration). Text is rendered with TextBlock, never Label or ContentPresenter over a string, so '_' and '&' in names are not eaten as access keys. There is no CollectionViewSource and no view-side sorting.
components.key_interactions: The host cell must give the tree a bounded height (a star row, not Auto, not inside a StackPanel or ScrollViewer). Otherwise virtualization silently turns off and all 100k containers are realized. The hook logs the realized-container count so this fails loudly.

components.name: Window wiring
components.responsibility: On the completed branch of the scan ending (the block that already reads ScanResult.Store, about :370-430): build the root node, set FolderTree.ItemsSource to that single root, expand it, collapse TopLevelList, show FolderTree. On Cancel or failure: the existing flat ending, unchanged, no tree. At StartScan (about :194): set FolderTree.ItemsSource = null, drop the root node, collapse FolderTree, show TopLevelList, and make sure no MainWindow field still references the previous ScanResult, so two stores never coexist.
components.key_interactions: Consumes ScanResult.Store (src/FsAnalyser.Core/ScanResult.cs:38) only after Scan() has returned. The DispatcherTimer progress path, the live list refresh (~:302-307) and TopLevelTracker are untouched.

components.name: Hook tree mode
components.responsibility: New FSA_HOOK_MODE=tree. After the scan completes it walks FolderTree breadth-first to depth 4, expanding each folder with at most 1,000 children. Per row it logs depth, relative path, sibling order, raw OnDisk and Size, the node's display strings, and the text actually rendered by the realized container (TextBlock.Text) or null if not realized. FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=<relative path> opens that folder 5 times, collapsing between opens, and logs each timing and the realized-container count. FSA_HOOK_RELEASE=<second temp root> starts a second scan through the window's own start path after capturing a WeakReference to the first store, forces GC, and logs whether the first store is collectable. Then it closes the window.
components.key_interactions: Writes JSON lines to FSA_HOOK_LOG, loaded with DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS like the existing stop|throw|close modes. The rendered text is the assertion source. A row that is not realized in case A fails the case, so the check cannot degrade to reading the node.

components.name: Window cases for the tree
components.responsibility: Case A: a 4-level temp tree whose files are distinct whole multiples of 4 KiB (at least 4 KiB), plus a junction, a sparse or NTFS-compressed sibling, an empty folder, a folder holding only a subfolder chain, and names with '_' and '&'. Driven with tree mode, asserted for rows 1-4. Case B: a temp folder of 100,000 files (about 50 distinct 4 KiB-multiple sizes at the top, the rest empty), driven with FSA_HOOK_EXPAND, asserting rows 5. Case C: the release case. Case D: the existing StallRig responsiveness case re-run on this build for row 6, plus cancel and throw modes asserting no tree. Existing cases that read TopLevelList after a completed scan are moved to read the tree root's children.
components.key_interactions: Builds the hook through Update-Hook and StallRig through Update-StallRig, both via eng/dotnet.ps1. The report stays schema 1 through eng/read-window.ps1.

components.name: Slice design note
components.responsibility: Records what a later live-tree slice inherits: the tree is built only from a completed scan; TopLevelTracker is deliberately not retired; the store is deliberately not published before Finish (this answers SL-039-live-results.md:17-18,165 and SL-042-folder-totals.md:160-163); a cancelled scan shows no tree; a live tree first needs the Core read path named in the mid-scan-shares spike (per-folder immutable snapshots to depth 4, or a store published with a seqlock or epoch).
components.key_interactions: The architecture rule on the live store points here. Whoever lifts that rule must first build the read path this note names.

contracts.name: FolderTreeNode construction and expansion
contracts.notes: FolderTreeNode.Root(ScanStore) makes the root row: GetPath(root) as its label, rolled on-disk size and size, no share. The first expansion of a folder sets Children once to nodes built from store.ChildrenLargestFirst(entry), in that order, with OnDisk and Share taken verbatim from each ChildRow. Later expansions reuse the same array. The window never re-sorts. Ranking and share are by on-disk size; the Size column is informational.
contracts.error_cases: The caller passes only the store of a completed scan. A folder with ChildCount 0 (empty, unreadable, or a link) gets no placeholder and no expander. A parent with 0 rolled on-disk gives Share exactly 0 (Core rule, ScanStore.Rollup.cs:72), shown as '0.0 %' with a zero-width bar. A link or a later hardlink name shows its 0 charge as it stands.
contracts.auth_model: none (in-process, read-only over a store no thread is writing)

contracts.name: Results view after a scan
contracts.notes: Completed scan: FolderTree is visible with the root expanded and its children largest first by on-disk size. Each row shows name, on-disk size, size, a bar and a one-decimal percentage of its parent. The root shows its total with no share. Running scan: TopLevelList is live exactly as in SL-039 (sorted by bytes, no shares). At completion the rows can reorder, because the tree ranks by on-disk size. Cancelled or failed scan: TopLevelList, no shares, as today. Starting a new scan clears and releases the tree before the scan begins.
contracts.error_cases: A failed or cancelled scan never shows a tree, because its shares would be of an incomplete whole. Picking a new folder while a tree is shown releases the old tree and its store first.

contracts.name: FSA_HOOK_MODE=tree log
contracts.notes: Environment: FSA_HOOK_MODE=tree, FSA_HOOK_LOG=<file>, optional FSA_HOOK_EXPAND=<path relative to scan root>, optional FSA_HOOK_RELEASE=<second temp root>. Lines: {kind:'tree-row', depth, path, order, onDisk, size, onDiskText, sizeText, shareText, barWidth, rendered:{name,onDisk,size,share}|null}; {kind:'expand', path, open:1..5, cold:bool, ms, firstChild, realized}; {kind:'store-released', released:bool}. An open is timed from setting IsExpanded=true on the realized container to the first ContextIdle dispatcher callback after the first child container exists. Assertions use `rendered`, not the node strings. The listing covers only the test's own temp tree and goes to the hook's log, not the app's report.
contracts.error_cases: The hook logs {kind:'error', reason} and closes the window if the scan does not complete, FolderTree is not found, the FSA_HOOK_EXPAND path does not resolve to a folder row, or a case-A row is not realized.

contracts.name: --report schema 1
contracts.notes: Unchanged. Per Q-016 it holds totals and the root and never a listing, so the tree's rows are not added to it.

key_decisions.decision: The tree is built only from a completed scan's ScanResult.Store. While the scan runs the window keeps SL-039's live flat list; TopLevelTracker is not retired and the store is not published before Finish. Cancelled and failed scans show no tree.
key_decisions.rationale: Owed row 1 says the tree appears when the scan finishes. Both spikes on the live path were no-go (refresh median 84 ms and UI gap 866 ms; child above parent 10-21 times per scan). The build check notes that a tree shown only after the scan needs neither prerequisite. A share after Cancel would be of an incomplete whole (TopLevelRowText.cs:10), and cancel belongs to SC-002. A live tree later is an addition on a new Core read path; nothing here has to be undone.

key_decisions.decision: Use the stock WPF TreeView with hierarchical virtualization (IsVirtualizing, Recycling, Pixel scroll, fixed row height), not a custom flattened TreeListView.
key_decisions.rationale: It is the configuration that was measured: 816 MiB peak with the store loaded, flat over 5 collapse/expand cycles of a 100k folder, and a 230 ms median cold 100k expand (U-001). Replacing it later would change the node model (hierarchical Children and a data-bound IsExpanded), the hook's tree walk and the window cases, so the row 5 measurement decides it early (see the decidable disagreement).

key_decisions.decision: Children load lazily through a shared placeholder child. On the first expand they are built once from ChildrenLargestFirst, set with a single Children swap (one reset, never per-item Add), and kept until the next scan.
key_decisions.rationale: Only folders a person opens pay for the sort and the nodes. A single swap avoids 100k change notifications. Keeping the array makes re-expansion free, and memory was flat across repeated opens in the spike. The worst case is bounded by how many big folders one person opens by hand, against about 208 MiB of headroom (816 of 1024 MiB).

key_decisions.decision: Rows include files and links as well as folders, in the order ChildrenLargestFirst returns them. Only folders with ChildCount > 0 can be expanded.
key_decisions.rationale: Row 5's check opens a folder of 100,000 files, so files are rows. A large file sitting directly in a folder is also part of where the space went. Links are leaf rows with 0 charge and are never descended into.

key_decisions.decision: FolderTreeNode implements INotifyPropertyChanged and IsExpanded is bound TwoWay in the ItemContainerStyle. Display text is read from the store when a row is drawn.
key_decisions.rationale: With Recycling, expand state has to live on the data item or it follows recycled containers to the wrong rows. Binding to a class without INotifyPropertyChanged makes WPF hold PropertyDescriptor references that can keep a 650 MiB store alive into the next scan (recalled: KB938416).

key_decisions.decision: The share is shown as a one-decimal percentage plus a bar of Share times a fixed track width, taken verbatim from ChildRow.Share. The root has no share. The ranking key and the share basis are on-disk size, and the column headers say so.
key_decisions.rationale: Row 3 names both the bar and one decimal place. The number is already computed and tested in Core, so the window only formats it. On-disk is the epic's ranking basis: U-019 shows online-only OneDrive data reads 0 on disk and so is not counted as local.

key_decisions.decision: Rows 1-4 are asserted from the text the tree actually renders (TextBlock.Text of realized containers) logged by a new FSA_HOOK_MODE=tree. The app's --report stays schema 1 with no listing.
key_decisions.rationale: Q-016 decided the report never holds a listing, and the hook is test-only code outside FsAnalyser.slnx. Reading rendered text catches a wrong XAML binding path, which WPF swallows silently. Reading node properties by reflection would only re-test the formatter.

key_decisions.decision: Row 5 asserts under 0.5 s on every one of the 5 opens, and open 1 (cold: JIT, sort, node build) is logged and asserted separately from opens 2-5, which reuse the cached array. The realized-container count is logged so virtualization loss fails the case.
key_decisions.rationale: A person opens a folder once, which is the cold case. Averaging in four warm re-opens would hide it. A 100k realized count is the signature of a TreeView in an unbounded-height host.

key_decisions.decision: Starting a scan sets FolderTree.ItemsSource to null and drops the root node and any MainWindow reference to the previous ScanResult before the new scan begins. A hook WeakReference check verifies the old store is collectable.
key_decisions.rationale: One 5M-entry store is 652 MiB and the tree peak is 816 MiB, so a second store would breach the 1 GiB budget. The proposal left this must-verify because nobody checked whether MainWindow keeps the last result in a field.

key_decisions.decision: Expansion runs synchronously on the UI thread (ChildrenLargestFirst plus node build). If row 5 misses 0.5 s, the sort moves to a worker and the Children swap returns to the dispatcher.
key_decisions.rationale: U-001 measured a 230 ms median cold expand. Synchronous keeps 'expand to first screen drawn' one uninterrupted interval. The store is not written after Finish, so a worker read is safe if it is needed.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Taken whole (lazy TreeView over the finished store, hook-verified) with three changes: the hook asserts rendered text, row 5 asserts cold and warm opens separately, and store release becomes a WeakReference case. The MVCC snapshot pattern travelled inside this proposal and is carried as cross_domain_transfer. No crossdomain or expert proposal was run.

payload.coherence_check: ONE PROPOSAL, NO COMPOSITION TO CHECK, and nothing here has survived a disagreement. The reviewer should argue with it first. What I checked at the seams between the proposal and reality: (1) Error contract: cancelled and failed scans keep today's flat ending, and the tree appears only for a completed scan, so there is one contract and it matches the existing ending. (2) Consistency: no thread writes the store the tree reads, because ScanResult.Store exists only after Scan() returns and Run._store is private. This was the invariant both no-go spikes broke, and this design never reads the live store. (3) Ordering seam: the live flat list sorts by bytes and the tree by on-disk, so rows can reorder at hand-off. The proposal accepted this, and I kept it and recorded it in the contract, because no owed row covers the mid-scan list. (4) Memory seam: the 816 MiB spike measured one store plus the tree, so a retained old store is a budget breach; I turned the proposal's must-verify into a WeakReference case. (5) Test-authority seam: the proposal read node properties by reflection, which cannot see a broken binding. I changed that to rendered text with a fail-if-not-realized rule. (6) Timing seam: the proposal's 5 opens mixed one cold and four warm; I split them. (7) The proposal's shared static placeholder node holds no store, so no rule bans static node fields. Architecture rules: I wrote two and dropped two candidates. Dropped: a regex for a static field holding ScanStore or ScanResult (the WeakReference case is the real check and the regex is easily dodged), and a XAML rule against IsVirtualizing=False (a line-scoped regex cannot scope to the tree; the realized-container count covers it at runtime). The Core rule excepts src/FsAnalyser.Core/ScanResult.cs, but the survey cited ScanResult.cs without its directory. If that path is wrong the rule will fire loudly on the legitimate `public required ScanStore Store`, and the builder must correct the except path (a loud false positive, not a silent one). Per Q-009 and Q-010 these rules are appended to the existing rules file on trunk, not created again. Not contested by anyone: the choice of stock TreeView (only the U-001 230 ms figure and the memory spike back it, and neither timed the published exe's hook path), the 4 KiB-multiple test files, and the row 6 argument that nothing here touches the mid-scan path (the StartScan release of a large store and the hand-off are the only new work near a scan, and case 14 covers both).

architecture_rules.name: the folder tree shows Core's order and never re-sorts or mutates children item by item
architecture_rules.because: ChildrenLargestFirst owns the order (on-disk size, then entry order). A second sort in the window with another key, such as the bytes sort the flat list uses, silently disagrees with Core and with row 2. Per-item edits to Children raise one change notification per row, which cannot meet row 5 at 100,000 children. Children is replaced once, as a whole array.

architecture_rules.name: Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends
architecture_rules.because: Rollups are posted while the scanner writes, and reading them from another thread is unsupported (SL-042 doc). The mid-scan-shares spike measured child above parent 10-21 times per scan and children summing above the parent about 400 times. ScanResult.Store, set when Scan() returns, is the only sanctioned way to a store. A live tree needs a consistent read path first (immutable per-folder snapshots, or a seqlock or epoch), and whoever builds it must change this rule on purpose.

cases.behaviour: show the tree when a scan completes (row 1)
cases.shape: the picked folder contains subfolders and files and the scan runs to the end
cases.why: The completed branch swaps TopLevelList for FolderTree and expands the root. A wrong swap leaves the flat list showing, or a tree with no root label. Existing cases that read TopLevelList after completion must move to the tree root's children.

cases.behaviour: order a folder's children largest first (row 2)
cases.shape: siblings whose byte size order differs from their on-disk order (a sparse or NTFS-compressed file bigger in bytes than a sibling but smaller on disk)
cases.why: The flat list sorts by bytes; the tree must rank by on-disk. A copied sort key passes any tree where the two orders agree. Use distinct 4 KiB-multiple sizes so no ties make the expected order ambiguous.

cases.shape: a folder three levels deep, a folder that holds only a subfolder chain and no files of its own, and the root
cases.why: The total must include everything below, including folders with no direct files. The root's rolled size must equal the sum of its visible children plus its own files.

cases.behaviour: show a folder with nothing readable in it (row 4)
cases.why: ChildCount 0 must give a leaf with no placeholder and no expander. An expander over nothing makes the person open a folder that shows nothing. It also stands for unreadable folders, which the store records with ChildCount 0.

cases.shape: a junction (and a symbolic link) inside the scanned tree
cases.why: Links are not followed and add 0. The tree must show them as non-expandable rows with 0 size, and must not offer to open the folder they point to, which would show bytes already counted elsewhere.

cases.behaviour: show a share of a zero parent (row 3)
cases.shape: a parent whose rolled on-disk is 0 but which has children (for example 100,000 empty files)
cases.why: Core returns Share exactly 0 there. The formatter must show '0.0 %' and a zero-width bar, with no NaN, no divide, and no bar wider than its track.

cases.behaviour: format a share to one decimal (row 3)
cases.shape: a share with no terminating decimal (1/3, 2/3) and a nonzero share small enough to round to 0.0 %
cases.why: The hand-computed check is to one decimal place. The formatter must round the way the test expects and use the same culture rule as the existing size text. A tiny nonzero share shows '0.0 %' by decision, so it must not throw or show a negative or empty bar.

cases.shape: folder and file names containing '_' and '&', and a name too long for its column
cases.why: WPF treats '_' as an access key marker in Label and ContentPresenter text and drops it. A wrong template element would show 'myfolder' for 'my_folder'. Only the rendered text, not the node string, can show this.

cases.shape: 100,000 files directly in one folder, about 50 of them distinct 4 KiB multiples and the rest empty (a tie block at 0), opened cold and then re-opened 4 times after collapsing
cases.why: The first open pays JIT, the sort and the node build; opens 2-5 reuse the cached array. Every open must be under 0.5 s and open 1 is the one that matters. The realized-container count must stay small (virtualization on), or the TreeView sits in an unbounded-height host and all 100k containers exist.

cases.behaviour: keep expand state through recycling and re-expansion (row 2)
cases.shape: a folder with more children than fit on screen, one child expanded, then the parent collapsed and re-expanded, and the list scrolled away and back
cases.why: With Recycling, IsExpanded must live on the data item. If it lives on the container the expanded state jumps to a different row, and the wrong folder appears open under the wrong parent. The order and totals must also be unchanged after re-expansion.

cases.behaviour: start a second scan while a tree is shown (rows 1 and 6)
cases.shape: a tree with an expanded large folder is on screen, then a new folder is picked
cases.why: StartScan must clear the tree and drop every reference to the old ScanResult before the new scan builds. Otherwise two 650 MiB stores coexist and pass 1 GiB. The old store must be collectable after a forced GC, and the new tree must show only the new root.

cases.behaviour: end a scan without a tree (row 1)
cases.shape: the scan is cancelled (hook mode stop) or fails (hook mode throw)
cases.why: The ending has three branches. Showing a tree on a cancelled or failed scan would show shares of an incomplete whole. The flat ending must be unchanged and FolderTree must stay collapsed.

cases.behaviour: keep the window responsive during a scan (row 6)
cases.shape: a scan of a large folder, with the window moved and resized during it, then the completion hand-off, then a new scan starting over a large shown tree
cases.why: This slice adds nothing to the mid-scan path, but it adds the hand-off (building the root, swapping controls) and the StartScan release of a large tree and store. StallRig re-run on this build confirms none of those causes 'Not Responding'.

cases.behaviour: count a hardlinked file in the tree
cases.shape: two names of one file in different folders
cases.why: Counting once is a Core rule, tested in Core.Tests on real NTFS trees (ScanStoreRollupTests, SL-042). The tree shows each ChildRow verbatim and does no accounting of its own. The second name shows 0 by design. A window case would only re-test Core through a slower path.

cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Readers only ever see a committed, immutable snapshot and never the writer's in-flight state. When a newer version arrives the old snapshot is dropped, not patched. Here the tree reads only the ScanResult.Store handed over when Scan() returns, and discards it when the next scan starts.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: Both no-go spikes are the classic failures of reading a live write set: torn reads (child above parent) and refreshing a view under a writer (UI stalls). Reading only a committed snapshot removes both by construction. The cost is seeing nothing below level 1 until the scan ends, which owed row 1 accepts. This is a genuine fit with a concrete cost, not a forced analogy.

invariants.precondition: No thread writes the store the tree reads
invariants.evidence: ScanResult.Store exists only after Scan() returns, and Run._store is private (mid-scan-shares spike, deviation (a); build check C6 cites ScanResult.cs:38). The architecture rule on Scanner-side publishing keeps it that way.

invariants.precondition: Each scan writes a fresh store, so a new scan never changes the snapshot under the tree
invariants.evidence: The scanner's Run holds its own private ScanStore per run (mid-scan-shares spike, deviation (a)).

invariants.precondition: The snapshot is complete, so shares are of the whole
invariants.evidence: For completed scans the root rollup equals ScanResult.Totals (build check C1, ScanResult.cs:20). It fails for cancelled scans, which is why they get no tree.

invariants.precondition: The old snapshot is released before the next is built, so one store is in memory against the 1 GiB budget
invariants.evidence: Not measured. It depends on MainWindow holding no field that references the previous ScanResult and on the tree being cleared at StartScan. The build check did not look at this. Discharged by the WeakReference case (start a second scan while a tree is shown).

decidable_disagreements.question: Does a stock virtualizing TreeView show the first screen of a 100,000-child folder in under 0.5 s, cold, in the published exe, timed by the hook (IsExpanded=true to ContextIdle after the first child container)?
decidable_disagreements.positions: Proposal: yes, a synchronous expand fits (U-001 measured a 230 ms cold median with 94 containers, and the memory spike used this exact tree config), with the sort on a worker as the cheap fallback. Against: neither measurement timed the hook's interval in the published exe, and the memory spike scrolled but did not time the open, so the stock TreeView's container generation for 100k items is unmeasured on this path. If the worker fallback also misses 0.5 s, the answer is a flattened list control.

taste_disagreements: Expandable tree versus a flat drill-down list. The FolderSizes page cited describes both shapes. The proposal takes the tree so the path from the drive stays in view.
Files shown as rows next to folders, versus folders only. Row 5's own check opens a folder of 100,000 files, which is why files are rows here.
FolderTreeRowText as its own class versus formatting properties on FolderTreeNode. This is layering, and nothing in the rules depends on it.
A nonzero share that rounds to zero shows '0.0 %' (matches a hand-computed check) versus '<0.1 %' (more honest to the person). The proposal keeps '0.0 %'.
Rows reorder at hand-off from the live flat list (by bytes) to the tree (by on-disk), versus re-sorting the live list by on-disk now. Left alone, since no owed row covers the mid-scan list.

prior_art.pattern: Disk-usage tree views come in two shapes: a tree whose child nodes collapse and expand, or a flat folder view that drills down. This slice takes the expandable tree.
Comparing logical with physical size in sortable lists. This supports showing both size and on-disk size on every row, ranked by on-disk size.
A subtree-percentage column drawn as a bar next to each row of the directory tree list.
A lazy-loading TreeView with a dummy child: each unexpanded node holds one placeholder so the expander shows, and the real children load on the first IsExpanded.
prior_art.where: Josh Smith, 'Simplifying the WPF TreeView by using the ViewModel pattern' (CodeProject, 2008)

prior_art.pattern: The Win32 TreeView equivalent: TVITEM.cChildren = I_CHILDRENCALLBACK shows the expand button without inserting children, which are filled in on TVN_ITEMEXPANDING.

Hierarchical UI virtualization in TreeView (.NET 4.5+): it needs VirtualizingPanel.IsVirtualizing and a height-constrained host. Recycling requires IsExpanded bound to the data item, and hosting the TreeView in a StackPanel or ScrollViewer quietly turns virtualization off.
Binding to a property of an object that does not implement INotifyPropertyChanged attaches PropertyDescriptor value-changed handlers held statically, which leaks the source object.
